next.reason: 1985 refuses an indexed WRITE with neither INVALID KEY nor an applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure; no other 1985 rule allows it. 2023 has no such syntax rule: the format leaves both phrases optional, and at run time §2023:9.1.14 GR1 sets the invalid key I-O status 'and, if enabled, the EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY exception condition is set to exist', §2023:9.1.14 GR3 runs any applicable exception processing statements, and §2023:9.1.14 GR4 'If the INVALID KEY phrase is not specified ... and there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement.' A compile-time refusal became an accepted program with a run-time exception condition (when enabled).
